pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks that all three existing rows are 0 and that the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test expects '★ Second item' with the other two unmarked.
'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects only those two, in id order.
'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order.
'AC-5' checks the 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on the starred view.
'AC-6' checks that Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__ all return 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. The 'AC-7' test asserts it.

findings.what: The spec's 'Empty table' state row (nothing listed, 'No items yet.', link to Starred only) has no test. Commit 972fb1b 'Follow-up edits' deleted 7 lines from test/starred.test.js, which left a stray double blank line where that test sat. The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. The 'Full list' test does not cover this state, because it runs with 3 items.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec, apart from the missing test for the Empty table state.
All 7 items are implemented and each is named by a test. The decisions are followed: the order is unchanged and the view is a query parameter. One state-table row (Empty table) has no test.
The Empty table state test was deleted in the last commit. The other tests assert behaviour. I did not run the tests; CI runs them.
The README describes ?show=starred. I found nothing stale.
The show parameter is validated with Object.hasOwn and the SQL is a fixed string, so I found no defect. The traffic route regex change is covered by tests/traffic-config.test.sh.
The title is HTML-escaped, the show value is allow-listed, and the SQL is built only from fixed strings. The change contains no review-directing instructions.
The change only adds a link and a ★ glyph to a plain HTML page. It has no CSS, components or layout.
